neighbours.label: water condensing out of the air: dew, mist, fog, condensation, drizzle and droplets (fires on the word or on the word just before it); flowing or drinking water, smoke and the metaphorical 'driving' stay low
fire: Beads of condensation ran down the inside of the tent.
By sunrise the grass was heavy with dew.
Thick fog rolled in from the bay and swallowed the bridge.
Her breath turned to mist in the frozen air.
Tiny droplets gathered on the cold pipe and dripped onto the floor.
The bathroom mirror fogged up as soon as the shower ran.
Humid air condensed on the chilled bottle within minutes.
A light drizzle hung over the harbour all morning.
quiet: Streaks of paint ran down the inside of the tent.
By sunrise the grass was heavy with fallen leaves.
Thick smoke rolled in from the bay and swallowed the bridge.
Her voice turned to a whisper in the frozen air.
Tiny pebbles gathered on the old pipe and rattled onto the floor.
The bathroom mirror cracked as soon as the shower ran.
Warm air circulated around the chilled bottle within minutes.
A light breeze blew over the harbour all morning.

notes: Card: ' cond' x7 (condensation), ' dro' x4 (droplets), ' acid', ' water', ' driving' (rain), 'coldest dew', 'morning dew', 'wreathed in clouds' (max 336); the + pole suppresses ' mist', ' dew', ' fog', ' dro', ' cond'.
